1.title: Loved in the Truth
1.context: The writer signs himself only as the elder, as in the letter before this one. Gaius is the only named recipient of the elder's letters; the New Testament names other men called Gaius, and this letter gives no way to identify its friend with any of them.
1.question: Whose love have you received that was located, as the elder puts it, in the truth?

1.title: That You May Enjoy Good Health
1.context: The prayer balances the sentence: the soul's prosperity is stated as known, the body's health is prayed for. It is one friend's real prayer for another, not a formula.
1.question: When you pray for a friend, do you pray for their health and circumstances as naturally as for their soul?

1.title: No Greater Joy
1.context: Traveling brothers carried the report both ways on the road. The elder's superlative is plain: no greater joy than hearing his children walk in the truth. The framing paragraph naming the elder's tradition and the book's undated place rides this closing scene.
1.question: Who would be overjoyed to hear a report about your walk, and what would they hear?

2.title: Faithful to Strangers
2.context: Faithful is hospitality's word here: a trust kept. The brothers were strangers to Gaius, so his welcome rested on the work they carried, not on friendship owed.
2.question: Is there a stranger doing God's work whom you could receive this week in some real way?

2.title: A Manner Worthy of God
2.context: The testimony about Gaius's love was delivered before the church, on the record. The sending standard is set by the Sender: provisions measured as worthy of God himself.
2.question: What would change in how you support God's workers if the standard were worthy of God rather than what is usual?

2.title: On Behalf of the Name
2.context: The travelers went out for the Name and accepted nothing from those outside the faith, so the whole weight of their support rested on the households of believers.
2.question: Why do you think accepting nothing from the Gentiles mattered to these travelers?

2.title: Fellow Workers for the Truth
2.context: Support is named as partnership: the host becomes a fellow worker for the truth. This open door is the counterpart to the shut door of the previous letter; both are the same elder's teaching in different settings.
2.question: Whose work for the truth are you already a fellow worker in, perhaps without naming it that?

3.title: Who Loves to Be First
3.context: Diotrephes is named with the one motive the text itself assigns him. An earlier letter to the church stands behind this one, mentioned and not shown.
3.question: Where in your own life does loving to be first get in the way of receiving instruction?

3.title: Putting Them Out of the Church
3.context: The elder's remedy is stated as intent if he comes. The list is his report: slander, the brothers refused, the willing forbidden, members expelled for wanting to welcome.
3.question: What does it cost a church when its door is controlled by one person's rank?

3.title: Do Not Imitate What Is Evil
3.context: The rule for reading the letter's two examples: imitate good, not evil. Its second half is stated at full strength, doing good as the mark of being of God.
3.question: Whose example are you imitating most closely right now, and is it the good one?

3.title: A Good Testimony from Everyone
3.context: Demetrius is commended by a threefold testimony: everyone, the truth itself, and the elder's own witness. The letter does not say whether he carries it.
3.question: If your testimony were written by everyone who knows you, what would it say?

3.title: Greet Them by Name
3.context: The close refuses pen and ink for face to face, as the previous letter refused paper and ink. The last instruction keeps the smallest kindness: greet each of our friends there by name.
3.question: Who in your circle needs to be greeted by name this week, not just included in a general hello?
